description:
Add frequency-selective (multipath) fading channels so coded-modulation chains can be evaluated over realistic broadcast and cellular channels, such as DVB-T2 TU6 or 3GPP TDL profiles, in addition to flat fading.

## Background

The channel stages in `crates/gf2-sim/src/channels/` model AWGN and frequency-flat Rayleigh and Rician fading, each drawing a fixed number of ChaCha20 words per symbol so the executor can seek any frame deterministically. A tapped-delay-line channel has inter-symbol memory, so it needs either an OFDM-style modulator and demodulator, giving one flat gain per subcarrier, or a time-domain channel with an equalizer. Either choice affects the stage graph and the per-frame RNG layout. `gf2-coding`'s `ChannelModel` trait accepts multipath models without structural change.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A tapped-delay-line channel with a configurable power-delay profile exists, with at least one standard profile (for example DVB-T2 TU6 or a 3GPP TDL profile) provided as a preset.
- [hard] REQ-02: Received symbols reach the soft demapper with the per-symbol (or per-subcarrier) effective gain, so LLRs use the coherent fading metric.
- [hard] REQ-03: Frame outputs are byte-identical across worker counts at a fixed seed, consistent with the executor's per-frame seek contract.
- [hard] REQ-04: The empirical channel statistics (average tap powers and the frequency correlation implied by the delay profile) match the configured profile within a stated tolerance in a statistical test.
- [hard] REQ-05: A coded BER/FER sweep over the new channel runs end to end through the preset or graph API.

## Notes

Choosing between an OFDM front end and time-domain equalization is part of this issue's design. Doppler (time-varying taps) may be split out if the design warrants it.
title: Frequency-selective multipath channel models
